c.tagline: Ancient empires and chaos in India's capital.

taxi.fareNote: Meters often ignored; app cabs dominant

emergency.note: 100 (police) and 108 (ambulance) also work; English-speaking operators are common in Delhi.

hood_landmark.Connaught Place: colonial-era white colonnades circling Central Park
hood_landmark.Chandni Chowk: the Red Fort rising at the bazaar's eastern end
hood_landmark.Hauz Khas: Hauz Khas Fort and its medieval reservoir beside Deer Park
hood_landmark.Karol Bagh: Ajmal Khan Road's bustling shopping bazaar
hood_landmark.Saket: Select Citywalk mall, with the Qutub Minar close by

avoid.reason: Pervasive touts/scams around New Delhi station, Connaught Place and Paharganj (fake tourist offices, "hotel closed" taxi tricks); pickpocketing; women should take extra care at night

hood_desc: Connaught Place is the colonial-era circular commercial heart of New Delhi, packed with shops, restaurants and offices. It suits first-time visitors who want a central base with easy metro access and plenty to see on foot.

Chandni Chowk is the chaotic, sensory-overload heart of Old Delhi near the Red Fort, famous for street food, spice bazaars and narrow historic lanes. It is best for foodies and history lovers who embrace crowds and noise, not those seeking calm or comfort.
Hauz Khas is a trendy urban village in South Delhi wrapped around medieval ruins and a lake, full of boutiques, rooftop bars and cafes. It suits younger travelers, creatives and nightlife seekers.

Karol Bagh is a bustling mid-range district known for its jewelry, clothing and electronics markets plus value hotels. It suits budget to mid-range travelers who want good shopping and solid metro links.

Saket is an upscale, planned South Delhi neighborhood with big malls like Select Citywalk, corporate offices and proximity to Qutub Minar. It suits affluent shoppers, business travelers and families wanting modern amenities and a quieter feel.

water.note: Avoid tap water; use sealed bottled or purified water, including for brushing teeth.

transit.pay: Get a rechargeable smart card (increasingly the NCMC/One Delhi card) at any station customer-care counter for about ₹200 (~$2.40, including a refundable deposit), then tap in/out; QR-code tickets are also sold at machines and the DMRC app. Fares range roughly ₹10-60 (~$0.12-0.72) depending on distance.
transit.hours: Trains generally run from about 5-5:30am until 11:30pm-midnight, with services roughly every 3-10 minutes at peak.

transit.m: Airport Express (Orange Line) metro to New Delhi station, then short hop to Connaught Place, approx 20-25 min
Airport Express metro to Shivaji Stadium station (edge of Connaught Place), approx 25-30 min

food.name: Chole bhature
food.desc: Spiced chickpea curry with a puffed, deep-fried bhatura the size of a plate, plus pickled onions and green chilli. Delhi's heaviest and happiest breakfast.

places.name: Sita Ram Diwan Chand
places.note: Serving one dish only since 1950; paneer-stuffed bhature and a queue from opening.

places.name: Chache Di Hatti
places.note: North Campus institution, cash only, famously large portions.

places.name: Nagpal Chole Bhature
places.note: The student crowd's other favourite; go early before the batter runs out.

food.name: Butter chicken
food.desc: Tandoori chicken finished in a tomato, butter and cream gravy, invented in Delhi after Partition and best mopped up with naan or roomali roti.

places.name: Moti Mahal
places.note: The restaurant credited with creating butter chicken and dal makhani in the 1940s.

places.name: Havemore
places.note: Late-night Pandara Road stalwart, open until the early hours.

places.name: Aslam Chicken Corner
places.note: Butter chicken tikka drowned in melted butter and cream; street-side, standing room.

food.name: Chaat
food.desc: The whole savoury-snack family: golgappe filled with spiced water, aloo tikki, papdi chaat and dahi bhalla, layered with chutneys, yoghurt and chaat masala.

places.name: Ashok Chaat Corner
places.note: Chandni Chowk fixture for papdi chaat and aloo tikki; busy is the point.

places.name: Prabhu Chaat Bhandar
places.note: Near UPSC Bhawan; a long-running favourite for dahi bhalla and stuffed golgappe.

places.name: Bishan Swaroop Chaat Corner
places.note: Known for fruit chaat and aloo chaat cut and dressed in front of you.

food.name: Paranthas
food.desc: Stuffed flatbreads fried in ghee, filled with potato, cauliflower, paneer or even banana, and served with pickles, curd and a thin dal.

places.name: Paranthe Wali Gali
places.note: A whole lane of parantha shops, several trading since the 1870s; expect a wait.

places.name: Moolchand Parantha
places.note: Late-night roadside kiosk near Moolchand flyover, a Delhi 2am institution.

places.name: Babu Ram Devi Dayal Paranthe Wale
places.note: Over a century old, with more than a hundred parantha varieties including banana.

food.name: Old Delhi kebabs
food.desc: Mughlai grilling at its source: seekh and shami kebabs, mutton korma and nihari, eaten with khameeri roti in the lanes around the Jama Masjid.

places.name: Karim's
places.note: Founded 1913 by a family said to have cooked for the Mughal court; the classic first stop.

places.name: Al Jawahar
places.note: Karim's neighbour and rival, often quieter with equally good korma and kebabs.

places.name: Qureshi Kabab Corner
places.note: Street-side grill best after dark, especially strong on seekh and mutton burra.

food.name: Jalebi and daulat ki chaat
food.desc: Ghee-fried jalebi soaked in syrup, and daulat ki chaat, a winter-only froth of overnight-churned milk that dissolves the moment it hits your tongue.

places.name: Old Famous Jalebi Wala
places.note: On the Dariba Kalan corner since 1884; thick, ghee-fried jalebi sold by weight.

places.name: Kuremal Mohan Lal Kulfi Wale
places.note: Century-old kulfi maker known for stuffed fruit kulfi; a good hot-weather alternative.

places.name: Chandni Chowk winter vendors
places.note: Daulat ki chaat appears on handcarts only from roughly November to February.

food.name: Lassi
food.desc: Thick sweet or salted yoghurt drink served in a clay kulhad, often topped with malai and crushed pistachio. The standard antidote to Delhi chilli and heat.

places.name: Amritsari Lassi Wala
places.note: Near Fatehpuri Masjid; the malai-topped sweet lassi is the one to order.

places.name: Giani Di Hatti
places.note: Also famous for rabri faluda, a good stop after a kebab crawl.

places.name: Kuremal Mohan Lal Kulfi Wale
places.note: Lassi and kulfi from the same century-old counter in the old city.

food.name: Masala chai
food.desc: Black tea boiled with milk, sugar, ginger and cardamom, poured from a height at roadside stalls and drunk many times a day.

places.name: Chandni Chowk tea stalls
places.note: Kulhad chai from carts throughout the old city; cheapest and best in winter.

places.name: Cafe Lota
places.note: Regional Indian cooking at the Crafts Museum; a calm place for chai and snacks.

places.name: Depaul's
places.note: Tiny CP counter better known for its cold coffee, a Delhi ritual in its own right.

landmarks: India Gate
A monumental war memorial arch on a grand boulevard, especially striking illuminated at night.
Red Fort
A massive Mughal-era red sandstone fortress and UNESCO World Heritage Site, the historic heart of Old Delhi.
Qutub Minar
A soaring 73m carved sandstone minaret and UNESCO site, the tallest brick minaret in the world.
Humayun's Tomb
A grand Mughal garden-tomb of red sandstone and white marble that inspired the Taj Mahal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Lotus Temple
A striking lotus-flower-shaped Bahá'í House of Worship made of white marble petals, one of the most photographed modern buildings in India.
Akshardham Temple
An intricately carved sprawling Hindu temple complex famed for its architecture and evening light-and-water show.
Jama Masjid
India's largest mosque, with grand red sandstone and marble courtyards, offering sweeping views of Old Delhi from its minaret.
Rashtrapati Bhavan
The grand presidential palace with sweeping colonnades and Mughal Gardens, a centerpiece of colonial-era New Delhi.
Chandni Chowk
One of India's oldest and busiest markets, a chaotic, colorful maze of lanes perfect for vibrant street photography.
Raj Ghat
The serene black marble memorial to Mahatma Gandhi set in tranquil gardens, a place of quiet reflection and photography.

train.note: No international trains currently run from Delhi - the Delhi-Lahore Samjhauta Express to Pakistan has been suspended since 2019. Book domestic trains via IRCTC; main terminals are New Delhi (NDLS), Old Delhi, Hazrat Nizamuddin and Anand Vihar.

bus.note: The state-run DTC Delhi-Kathmandu AC coach departs from Dr. Ambedkar Terminal (Delhi Gate). Carry a passport or accepted ID for the India-Nepal border. Private operators also sell the route via redBus and similar sites.

ferry.note: Delhi is a landlocked inland city with no ferry service.

half.name: Agra
half.blurb: Home to the majestic Taj Mahal, a mighty red fort and grand Mughal monuments.

half.name: Damdama Lake
half.blurb: A tranquil lake amid the Aravalli hills popular for boating, birdwatching and easygoing outdoor escapes.

half.name: Sultanpur Bird Sanctuary
half.blurb: A wetland reserve near Gurgaon where migratory and resident birds gather around peaceful shallow lakes.

full.name: Neemrana
full.blurb: A restored hilltop fort-palace offering heritage rooms, terraced gardens and views over the Aravalli countryside.

full.name: Vrindavan
full.blurb: A sacred pilgrimage town linked to Krishna, filled with colorful temples and devotional riverside rituals.

full.name: Mathura
full.blurb: The revered birthplace of Krishna, dotted with ancient temples and lively ghats along the Yamuna.
